title: MacNeal and Harder's straight cantilever beam
model: a 6.0 x 0.2 x 0.1 beam, E 1.0e7 and nu 0.30 stated by the study (its units read as mm and MPa), clamped at x = 0 and loaded on its free end by a unit force along each axis and a unit moment about its length, one study each; 0.05 elements (two through the depth, against the paper's one); the free end's motion from probe_study's rigid fit of the face

extension.source: MacNeal & Harder, A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20, Table 3 (straight beam, extension)
extension.reason: F L / (E A) exactly, less only what the clamp holds of the root's Poisson contraction, a few hundredths of a percent over a beam 60 times its depth; a quadratic tet carries a constant strain exactly

in_plane_shear.source: MacNeal & Harder, A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20, Table 3 (straight beam, in-plane shear)
in_plane_shear.reason: bending plus shear across the 0.2 width; the clamp holds the root's Poisson contraction and warping, which the beam theory leaves free, a few tenths of a percent at L/h = 30 (cantilever's percent at L/h = 10, falling with h/L), and at 0.05 the mesh error is a tenth of that

out_of_plane_shear.source: MacNeal & Harder, A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20, Table 3 (straight beam, out-of-plane shear)
out_of_plane_shear.reason: as in-plane, across the 0.1 depth (L/h = 60), with two quadratic elements through it: the root's held contraction and the mesh together a few tenths of a percent

twist.source: MacNeal & Harder, A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20, Table 3 (straight beam, twist: unit moment, the end's rotation)
twist.reason: Saint-Venant torsion of a 2:1 rectangle, T L / (k1 b t^3 G) with k1 = 0.229 (Timoshenko & Goodier, ch. 10), is 0.0341: the published value is 6 % under the solid's answer, which a fine mesh converges to
twist.known_failure: the solid converges to Saint-Venant's 0.0341 rad (0.0312, 0.0334 and 0.0341 at 0.1, 0.05 and 0.025 elements), 6 % over the published 0.03208, which the paper gives without its derivation; the miss is the target's distance from the closed form, not the element's
